Java's default trust store includes roots that signed weak eMudhra intermediates, so a Java client could be fooled when it connects out. Keycloak has no way out: only the internal networks auth-front (Traefik) and db-auth (postgres-auth), whose certificates come from AetherSpark's own CA, and its database client checks against that root only. Red Hat marks it won't fix; the Keycloak base moves only with Ostium's next notice (D-008, O-035 lists it).

Uncontrolled memory allocation when guava's compact maps are deserialized. Keycloak reads requests as JSON and forms; Java serialization happens only between cluster nodes, and AetherSpark's Keycloak runs as one node with cache=local (no cluster port). Fixed in guava 33.7.2, not yet in a Keycloak release Ostium has noticed (O-035).

The system SQLite library, used in the image only by the package manager's database (rpm never runs in the container). Keycloak is Java and never loads it; the flaw needs a crafted FTS5 table and query. No fixed package yet (O-035 lists it).

The system SQLite library, used in the image only by the package manager's database (rpm never runs in the container). Keycloak is Java and never loads it; the flaw needs a crafted database file opened with FTS5 secure-delete. No fixed package yet (O-035 lists it).

The system SQLite library, used in the image only by the package manager's database (rpm never runs in the container). Keycloak is Java and never loads it; the flaw needs a crafted changeset for SQLite's session extension. No fixed package yet (O-035 lists it).

The SQLite command line's recovery command on a crafted database; the image has no use for it, rpm never runs in the container, and Keycloak (Java) never loads the system SQLite library. No fixed package yet (O-035 lists it).

CVE-2026-128089: excessive memory and CPU when dnspython's text parser reads a crafted WKS record from zone-file text. The LLM trial's model server reads no zone files: it answers the owner's chat requests only, on the internal llm network, with no port and no way out. Fixed in dnspython 2.9.2; NVIDIA has no rebuilt image yet. Ends with the image's other exceptions.

No fixed Alpine package yet; a rebuild picks up the fix, and the scan then reports this entry as stale.

Remote code execution in the JVM through crafted input, only on x86-64 CPUs with AVX-512 VBMI (Red Hat, 2026-11-17; ARM64 not known to be affected). The desktop's CPU (Intel Core i7-9700) has no AVX-512 at all, and the Spark is ARM64. This exception holds only while the stack runs on no CPU with AVX-512 VBMI (Intel Ice Lake or later, AMD Zen 4 or later). Two weeks, not four: Red Hat's analysis is still preliminary. No fixed Red Hat package yet; a fixed Keycloak image comes through Ostium's notice (ADR-0009 amendment 3, security-first rule).

Java's Kerberos acceptor mishandles cross-realm tickets. Keycloak here accepts no Kerberos tickets: no Kerberos user federation, and both realms sign in with their own flows (browser-security-key, browser-2fa), which have no Kerberos step. No fixed Red Hat package yet; a fixed Keycloak image comes through Ostium's notice (ADR-0009 amendment 3, security-first rule).

Java's TLS client completes a handshake with a server that sends no certificate (needs a man in the middle). Keycloak's only TLS client connection is JDBC to postgres-auth on the internal db-auth network, which only postgres-auth and Keycloak join. No fixed Red Hat package yet; a fixed Keycloak image comes through Ostium's notice (ADR-0009 amendment 3, security-first rule).

C2 JIT miscomputes integer-compression ranges (out-of-bounds access); exploiting it needs untrusted bytecode or steered compiled code. Keycloak runs only its own code, no scripts or providers from users. No fixed Red Hat package yet; a fixed Keycloak image comes through Ostium's notice (ADR-0009 amendment 3, security-first rule).

The Vector API's mask index check narrows large offsets (out-of-bounds access); exploiting it needs untrusted offsets passed into vector code. Keycloak runs only its own code. No fixed Red Hat package yet; a fixed Keycloak image comes through Ostium's notice (ADR-0009 amendment 3, security-first rule).
